messages:
tess liu: CI red on PR 5248 — docker push failing in finalize step after a Dockerfile symlink/chown tweak. Seen on both canary and main runners. Example log:
```
2026-03-12T12:34:56Z finalizing manifest upload
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
error: manifest finalize: access denied
```
Anyone seen this pattern recently? image: registry.redwood-inference.com/dev/worker:pr-5248

ci-bot: Build #5248 (branch/pr/5248) failed during push stage (exit 1). Logs uploaded: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/5248/log

omar gonzalez: did we rotate the registry token for the canaries last night? :thinking: if the push fails on finalize it can be creds or a broken upload session (cache/partial blob)

kevin park: FYI I merged the symlink -> chown change in #5239 earlier. It touched how we `ADD` and set owner for /app. Might change layer digests which could hit cache edge cases with our registry proxy.

tess liu: right — the chown was to fix permissions for the runner. I can revert but want to confirm root cause first. quick triage: can someone try a CI rerun with cache disabled for the push step? like set `CI_DOCKER_NO_CACHE=true` or pass `--no-cache` to buildx.

rina singh: also check the builder service account token expiry at the registry side. In past we saw a token TTL mismatch cause 401 on finalize even though blob upload succeeded. @ci-oncall can you check registry auth logs for subject `ci-builder@redwood` around 12:30 UTC?

ci-oncall: ACK. I'll tail auth logs and kick a rerun. scheduling rerun now with NO_CACHE and fresh docker config: rerun id 2951234575

omar gonzalez: while rerun runs, small repro locally: `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t registry.redwood-inference.com/dev/worker:pr-5248 --push . --no-cache` — if that succeeds it's auth. if it fails with same 401, try `export DOCKER_CLI_EXPERIMENTAL=enabled` + `--progress=plain` to get full response from registry.

tess liu: thanks. also adding a quick diagnostic: can we log the `Authorization` header hash on registry side? if tokens are rotated we can confirm mismatch.

ci-oncall: rerun completed at 2951234589 — result: SUCCESS with `--no-cache` flag. So push works without cache. Failing build used cached layers.

kevin park: that suggests cache+auth interaction — maybe cached layer upload resume attempted with stale session id. We should prevent resuming cached uploads when token TTL < X. I'll open a follow-up issue to invalidate cached upload sessions on token rotation.

tess liu: for now I'll back out the chown change from #5239 and reapply with a build step that forces new layers (so no resume). Opening quick PR to revert + reapply in safer way. cc @omar @rina

omar gonzalez: sounds good. also adding CI check — if push returns 401 on finalize, fail fast and auto-rerun once with `--no-cache` and alert owner. Cuts the manual triage loop.

tess liu: perfect. thanks everyone. marking this thread resolved after PR lands. :white_check_mark:
